definitions.explanation: Describes a face or complexion that looks unhealthily pale, often due to illness, shock, or fear.
Describes a faint, cold, bluish-white light or color.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{青白|あおじろ}い{顔|かお}で{立|た}っていた。
examples.english: He was standing there with a pale face.

examples.japanese: {熱|ねつ}があるのか、{朝|あさ}から{顔色|かおいろ}が{青白|あおじろ}かった。
examples.english: Perhaps he had a fever — his complexion was pale since morning.

examples.japanese: {月|つき}が{青白|あおじろ}く{光|ひか}っていた。
examples.english: The moon shone with a pale bluish light.

examples.japanese: {蛍光灯|けいこうとう}の{青白|あおじろ}い{光|ひかり}が{部屋|へや}を{照|て}らしていた。
examples.english: The bluish-white light of the fluorescent lamp illuminated the room.

examples.japanese: {夜明|よあ}け{前|まえ}の{空|そら}が{青白|あおじろ}く{染|そ}まり{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The sky before dawn began to take on a pale bluish tinge.

notes:
An i-adjective. Compound of {青|あお} (blue) + {白|しろ}い (white).

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {青白|あおじろ}く
- Noun form: {青白|あおじろ}さ

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {顔|かお}が{青白|あおじろ}い (face is pale)
- {青白|あおじろ}い{光|ひかり} (pale/bluish-white light)
- {青白|あおじろ}い{肌|はだ} (pale skin)

When describing a person's complexion, {青白|あおじろ}い implies ill health or shock. It is not used as a compliment for fair skin — {色白|いろじろ} is used instead.
